policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Select A, move to the top of the visible button to prepare, only when the observed hand is not already prepared. Recognize a closed gripper with wrist height approximately 0.15 (including 0.154–0.155), wrist roughly 34–36 image units above the button, and a small horizontal offset as already prepared. This configuration takes precedence over apparent wrist/button image-center misalignment: the wrist is not the fingertips' contact point. Do not select A merely because those image centers differ. Once prepared, choose between B and C using the updated passage_count and the requested ordinal N from the goal. C must be initiated before the requested passage because button pressing takes approximately 25–35 recording time units. For a prepared hand, select C only when both conditions hold: the updated passage_count equals N-1, and a reliable motion-based estimate places the next target passage approximately 35 or fewer recording time units away. The count alone never authorizes C. Select B if passage_count is less than N-1, or if it equals N-1 but the estimated next passage is outside this window or its timing is uncertain. Estimate the upcoming arrival from the chronological cube motion shown at this step, accounting for slowing and reversal at endpoints. A useful estimate fits smooth periodic motion x(t)=a+b*cos(w*t)+c*sin(w*t) to the current interval's timestamped cube positions and finds its next crossing of the visible target x; do not extrapolate a near-zero endpoint velocity as constant. When the cube is moving away from the target after the preceding crossing, estimate the next crossing by including both the remaining travel to the endpoint and the return travel to the target. Slowing down or nearing an endpoint does not by itself authorize C. A fast endpoint turnaround can nevertheless be the press-launch time if the estimated next crossing is within the lead window and passage_count equals N-1; do not require that the cube already be moving toward the target. Select B while fewer than N-1 passages have completed, or while the requested next passage remains farther away than this lead window. Reevaluate after every B; remaining static can span several passages, so update memory from every shown frame. None of these menu options requires a supplied point; A and C concern the visible button. If motion timing is uncertain, default to B while refining the estimate from the next observations, rather than pressing on the wrong ordinal. If already stopped at the requested target, remain static. For other uncovered situations, prepare with A if necessary, otherwise remain static with B.

fields.name: passage_count
fields.description: Start at 0 for empty memory, otherwise use the incoming passage_count. Process all newly shown observations chronologically, starting with incoming last_side as the preceding side. Compute the sign of cube x minus target x. Each nonzero sign opposite to the preceding nonzero side increments the count once; then update the working side. Ignore exact equality until a nonzero side appears. Include observations during A and B, and count multiple crossings within one decision interval separately. Write the resulting count, without adding any predicted future passage from the command being selected. e.g. 2

fields.name: last_side
fields.description: The cube's most recently observed nonzero side of the target center, represented as -1 when cube x is smaller than target x and 1 when it is larger. If exactly equal, retain the preceding nonzero side; use 0 if none has yet been observed. Record the side at the decision's final observation, not the side expected after its selected command. e.g. -1
